title: Ibn Abbas
hook: the young cousin, prayed for to understand the religion, later the great interpreter (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, sent to Yemen with three steps for judging. Your line was: book, sunnah, reason. Did you slow down before one judgment? Day eight hundred thirty-six.

A jug of water has been set out. Nobody asked for it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, comes to wash, finds it waiting, and asks: who put this here? Someone tells him: Abdullah, the son of your uncle Abbas. A boy. He had noticed what would be needed and quietly set it out. And the Prophet, instead of a thank you, says a short prayer for him, one line that the boy will carry for the rest of his life. Today: Ibn Abbas.
screen: `A JUG OF WATER, SET OUT.` → `WHO PUT THIS HERE?` → `A ONE-LINE PRAYER FOR A BOY.`

segments.voice: Sahih al-Bukhari records the prayer: O God, give him understanding of the religion. In Arabic, the prayer asks that he be given fiqh in the religion, the word later used for the study of Islamic law. In another report in Bukhari, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet held him close and prayed: O God, teach him the book. So the boy was prayed for in both ways: for understanding, and for the Qur'an. Did it show? Bukhari keeps a scene that answers. Years later, Umar, now leading the community, used to bring young Ibn Abbas into his council with the older men who had fought at Badr. Some of them objected. Why does he sit with us, when we have sons his age? So one day Umar asked the whole group about the surah that begins: when the help of God comes, and the victory. Some said it tells us to praise God and seek His forgiveness when victory comes. Others said nothing. Then Umar turned to Ibn Abbas. Is that what you say too? No, he said. It was the sign of the Prophet's own approaching death, given to him by God. When the victory comes, your work is done; praise your Lord and ask forgiveness. Umar answered: I know nothing of it except what you have said. The older men gave the plain meaning, and it was true. The young man saw what the surah was pointing to. Tradition remembers Ibn Abbas as an interpreter of the Qur'an. It started with a jug of water and a one-line prayer. Understanding, prayed for.
screen: `O GOD, GIVE HIM UNDERSTANDING.` · `O GOD, TEACH HIM THE BOOK.` · `UMAR'S QUESTION ABOUT SURAH 110.` · `THE YOUNG MAN UNDERSTOOD.` · then, large: `UNDERSTANDING PRAYED FOR.`

segments.voice: The practice: study one verse's meaning. Settle, and breathe. Take one short verse, maybe the first line of surah one hundred ten, when the help of God comes, and the victory. Say it once, slowly. Then ask Ibn Abbas's kind of question: not only what does it say, but what is it doing? Who is it speaking to? What moment is it for? Sit with that question, without hurrying to an answer. If you pray, you can ask, as the Prophet asked for him, for understanding. The bell holds the time.

Ibn Abbas. Abdullah, son of the Prophet's uncle Abbas, prayed for as a boy to understand the religion and the book, and remembered as an interpreter of the Qur'an. Today's word, and the last of the early believers.

Your line: understanding prayed for. Today, read one verse twice and ask what it is doing, not only what it says. Tomorrow the path turns to the later companions and their stories. Day eight hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Abdullah ibn Abbas as a companion known for explaining the Qur'an, and retell the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari where the Prophet prayed for him to be given understanding of the religion.

fork.setup: you are the Prophet. you step out to wash for prayer and find water already set out for you. a boy put it there. what do you do?
options: thank him and send him home.
pray for him: O God, give him understanding of the religion.
tell him to ask first next time.
fork.reveal: Bukhari records the one-line prayer for understanding. tradition remembers the boy as an interpreter of the Qur'an.

original.note: Arabic: 'understanding'; the word in the prayer 'give him understanding of the religion', and later the name for Islamic law.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ibn Abbas was just a relative of the Prophet.
what it means: he was prayed for as a boy to understand, and older men came to defer to his reading.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's report of Umar's council and surah 110, read as a sign of the Prophet's approaching death.
recall: the one who gives the call to prayer

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 143 (the water for washing; O God, give him understanding of the religion)
Sahih al-Bukhari 75 (O God, teach him the book)

notes: Audit: 'The older men had read the words; the young man had understood' belittled the Badr companions, whose reading is also accepted; now says their plain meaning was true and Ibn Abbas saw what the surah pointed to.
Last day of the part 'Early believers (823–836)'; the carry points to the next part, later companions.
Hadith numbers cited from memory; confirm Bukhari 143, 75 and 4970.
Bukhari 143 has 'faqqihhu fid-din'; the original note links it to the root of fiqh. Confirm.
Surah 110 verses paraphrased, not quoted from Pickthall.
In Bukhari 4970 the objecting men are not named individually ('some of them' / Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf in some versions); kept general.

Editor: Bukhari 143 places the water at his washing, not 'by the door' before prayer, so hook, screen and fork were adjusted; cut the root/etymology claim and the 'prayed for twice' count (the two reports may be one event).
